Title: Arbitrary Code Execution via eval() on unsanitized config parameter metric_agg
Analysis:
The vulnerability is located in `torch_geometric/graphgym/utils/agg_runs.py` at line 110 and line 237. The code parses user-influenced configurations via YACS config `cfg.metric_agg` and passes it directly into a dynamic `eval()` call. Specifically, the code formats a string `\"performance_np.{}()\".format(cfg.metric_agg)` and evaluates it.
If an attacker can control `cfg.metric_agg` (e.g. by setting `metric_agg` in a `.yaml` config file or via command-line options parsed by `parse_args()`), they can inject arbitrary Python code which will be executed in the context of the running application.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
An attacker could run `main.py` (which parses arguments and loads user-controlled YAML configuration) and supply an option or a configuration file that sets:
`metric_agg: "__import__('os').system('id')"`

When `agg_runs()` is called (either at the end of `main.py` or directly by user tools), it executes the expression:
`eval("performance_np.__import__('os').system('id')()")`
resulting in Arbitrary Code Execution (ACE) / Remote Command Execution (RCE).

Title: Arbitrary Code Execution via eval() in agg_batch function on metric_agg config parameter
Analysis:
The vulnerability is located in `torch_geometric/graphgym/utils/agg_runs.py` at line 237. In the `agg_batch` function, the YACS configuration parameter `cfg.metric_agg` is directly formatted into a string and evaluated with `eval()`.
If an attacker controls this parameter via the config file or command-line options, they can achieve arbitrary Python code execution.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
Setting `cfg.metric_agg` to `\"__import__('os').system('id')\"` triggers the execution of arbitrary system commands.
`eval(\"performance_np.__import__('os').system('id')()\")`
Snippet:
performance_np = np.array(  # noqa
                        [stats[metric] for stats in dict_stats])
                    dict_stats = dict_stats[eval("performance_np.{}()".format(
                        cfg.metric_agg))]
